rendering.persona_description: Rahul is a 52-year-old warehouse operations supervisor who has run the same distribution floor for almost twenty years. He's known among his crew as a stickler who keeps a spotless office and won't touch the shared coffee pot. Outside work he likes fixing up an old truck in his garage, though lately he does it in gloves he wipes down between uses.
rendering.clinical_context: Rahul has obsessive-compulsive disorder centered on contamination, particularly fears involving hospitals, medical waste, chemicals, and money he considers 'dirty.' He was diagnosed about four years ago after his wife pushed him to see someone when his handwashing routines started taking over the bathroom schedule at home. He is currently partway through a course of exposure and response prevention therapy but has been telling his wife he's not sure it's worth continuing.
rendering.behavioral_description: Rahul talks in short, flat statements and gets sharp or sarcastic when he feels cornered or lectured. He states his contamination beliefs as plain fact and treats any suggestion that they might be exaggerated as an insult to his intelligence. He'll answer questions but pushes back hard on anything that sounds like advice, often turning it around to ask why he should trust the other party's judgment over his own senses.

traits.living_situation: lives with his wife in a house he has divided into 'clean' and 'dirty' zones
traits.help_seeking_orientation: reluctant, ambivalent, present in treatment mainly because his wife and doctor pushed him into it
traits.cognitive_style: rigid, literal, treats contamination fears as established fact rather than as beliefs open to question

clinical_history.current_treatment: currently in a course of exposure and response prevention therapy, considering stopping
clinical_history.history: Symptoms have been present for at least a decade but worsened noticeably four years ago after a hospital visit for a minor injury, which is when his wife insisted he get evaluated.

symptoms: excessive handwashing, especially after touching money or doorknobs
avoidance of surfaces he associates with hospitals or medical waste
mental division of the house into clean and dirty zones
repeated checking that contaminated items haven't been touched by others
reassurance-seeking from his wife about whether something is 'clean'
strong disgust reactions to perceived contamination
